messages:
marta: Heads-up — I sketched a small spike proposal for a "compact lease projection" to reduce per-prefix metadata and improve eviction fairness across slabs. brief sketch below; want sanity-checks before I turn it into an RFC.

raj: High-level ask: how is this different from the existing lease snapshot? sounds like a lossy projection we can use for eviction/admission decisions? :eyes:

marta: Exactly — the idea is to keep a tiny, monotonic projection for each prefix that encodes epoch + a compact token + a cheap hotness estimate. Runtime uses projection for admission/evict heuristics. Full lease metadata still exists for correctness-heavy paths (hand-off, write path).

tom: Two immediate concerns: 1) handoff correctness when projection is stale, 2) ABA or token re-use causing fairness inversion.

marta: Good points. Proposed properties: projection must be monotonic (we never reuse tokens for a given epoch window), and it must be stitchable into full lease when asked. Fallback on mismatch is the slow path but safe.

marta: Draft interface sketch:
```
// compact projection kept alongside full lease
struct CompactLease { epoch: u64, token: u64, hot_score: u8 }
fn project(prefix_id) -> Option<CompactLease>
// attempt to stitch projection into observed full lease, returns None if not stitchable
fn stitch(compact: &CompactLease, full_lease_id: LeaseId) -> Option<FullLease>
```

kevin: How does this interact with tombstones/compaction? if a prefix is erased and later re-created, token monotonicity must hold or we punish the new tenant.

marta: Plan: include an epoch high-bit that gets bumped on full-delete/rename. token monotonicity is only required within an epoch; when epoch increments projection is effectively reset. That means handbacks that cross epoch increments must consult sequencer / full-lease.

raj: Metrics we should track during canary: projection_hit_rate, token_mismatch_rate, eviction_reorders (cases where eviction decision reversed), and read-after-write_falls_to_full. Also instrument histograms by tenant size.

tom: Can we make admission use only projection but require a soft fallback if eviction reorders exceed threshold? e.g. if projection yields an eviction that later conflicts with full lease, we defer harder evictions for that tenant for N minutes.

marta: I like that. call it a "soft-grace window" for projection-driven evictions. default 2m, adjustable per-tenant. Adds complexity but reduces user-visible churn.

kevin: Ops-wise: migration path should be feature-flagged with canary nodes and a rollout that watches token_mismatch_rate < 0.1% and eviction_reorders < 0.05% before 50% traffic. Also need an emergency kill-switch that sets runtime to always consult full lease.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag compact-lease-projection set to canary=10% in cluster "prefetl" (by marta).

marta: Next steps (actionable): 1) turn this into an RFC with the interface + migration plan + metrics, 2) implement prototype in `prefetch/compact-lease` branch, 3) add dashboards for the metrics raj listed, 4) plan a canary rollout and ops runbook. I'll book a short sync Wed 10am to review the RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
